I have farmed my seven mu of land in Quzhou County for over thirty years, and I know what works here on the North China Plain. My wheat is already in the ground—I sowed it last October after running the rotary tiller, using Jimai 22, an improved variety that the seed shop always recommends and that has never let me down. I will give it four irrigations: the overwintering water, the jointing water, the heading water, and one at grain filling. I will spread compound fertilizer as basal and topdress with urea when the wheat greens up, because the soil here needs plenty of nitrogen to produce a good stand. I will also spray four times for weeds, aphids, and disease. If the spring weather cooperates, I expect about 1000 jin per mu. As soon as I harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant Denghai 605 hybrid maize directly into the stubble without ploughing again—no-tillage saves diesel, time, and labor, and the maize sprouts fast in the summer heat. I will irrigate the maize twice and spray three times for insects and weeds. I do not grow cotton or vegetables; I saw my neighbor lose money on chili last year when prices crashed, and the grain station always buys wheat and maize. This double-cropping system feeds my family and pays for my grandchildren’s school fees.
